# Freeth et al. — A Model of the Cosmos in the Antikythera Mechanism (2021)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** Tony Freeth et al., “A Model of the Cosmos in the Ancient Greek Antikythera Mechanism,” *Scientific Reports* 11 (2021): 5821, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-84310-w.

**Shortened note:** Freeth et al., “Model of the Cosmos,” {section/page}.

**Bibliography:** Freeth, Tony, David Higgon, Aris Dacanalis, Lindsay MacDonald, Myrto Georgakopoulou, and Adam Wojcik. “A Model of the Cosmos in the Ancient Greek Antikythera Mechanism.” *Scientific Reports* 11 (2021): 5821. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-84310-w.

## Essay use

Open reconstruction study for the front Cosmos display, planetary periods, nested rings, inscriptional evidence, and constraints imposed by missing fragments. Particularly useful for the essay's theme that a model may be rigorous, generative, and visibly provisional at once.

**Claim boundary:** the authors explicitly present an evidence-constrained model of the lost original and preserve uncertainty where the surviving evidence underdetermines reconstruction. That epistemic modesty is part of the source's value; a demonstrated replica would require evidence the paper does not claim to possess.

## Passage card — `freeth-et-al-2021-model-cosmos-q002` — Reconstruction is not a replica
^freeth-et-al-2021-model-cosmos-q002

> “Because of the loss of evidence, we cannot claim that our model is a replica of the original, but our solution to this convoluted 3D puzzle draws powerful support from the logic of our model and its exact match to the surviving evidence.”
